findings.title: The dshGo inject callback probes once and caches the bridge in scopedDshGo, so a reload/re-inject keeps a previously bound bridge.
verifiedAgainst: packages/mpd-dsh-adapter-plugin/src/index.ts (pre-fix callback at b0d9ecb7, lines 4252-4278; early return at 4256)
real cordis 4.1.0 shipped by the pinned harness 0.2.2-rc.1 (ctx.inject unload/re-run contract)
codeFacts: PRE-FIX: the callback opened with `if (scopedDshGo !== undefined && scopedDshGo !== null) return`, so a second firing never re-probed and never returned a cleanup.
cordis contract (registry.d.ts:104-111): `inject(deps, callback)` is 'unloaded and re-run whenever a required service changes'.

REAL-CORDIS RED PROOF on HEAD source: after provide(dshGo 1.0.9) -> dispose -> provide(dshGo 2.0.0) the adapter reported present=true, caps={app:'1.0.9'} — the stale bridge survived the unload AND the newer provide.
REAL-CORDIS GREEN PROOF on the fixed tree: present=false after the unload, then present=true caps={app:'2.0.0'} after the re-provide.

FIX SHAPE: each firing probes its own bridge into a local `bound`, publishes it to `scopedDshGo`, calls notifyDshGoBound(), and returns `() => { if (scopedDshGo === bound) scopedDshGo = undefined }` — an identity guard, so an older activation's unload can never clobber a newer binding.

PRESERVED: the guarded `scoped?.dshGo` property read (THROWS on an undeclared service), the `scoped.get('dshGo', false)` probe, the onServiceBound notification path, and the absent-service behaviour (a bridgeless host never fires the callback: nothing registers, no polling, the consumer's ONE `dshGo=absent` line in packages/mpd-bundle-plugin is untouched).
findings.newTestArm: packages/mpd-dsh-adapter-plugin/test/adapter-dshgo-surface.test.ts :: 'a re-fired inject binds ITS OWN bridge, and an unload clears only its own binding' — fires the inject twice with distinct bridges, replays the OLDER unload last, and asserts the newer binding survives it.

findings.title: spawnSync returns status: null on the 180 s timeout, so a TIMEOUT is indistinguishable from a gate VIOLATION.
verifiedAgainst: node:child_process spawnSync semantics (timeout => error.code === 'ETIMEDOUT', status null, killSignal SIGTERM)
codeFacts: `GateRun` now carries `signal: string | null`, `error: string | null` (flattened `code: message`) and `timedOut: boolean` (`error.code === 'ETIMEDOUT'`, the authoritative timeout flag).
Every gate and control log line now renders `runDetail()`: `exit=… signal=… timedOut=… error=…`.
result.json carries `gate {exit, signal, timedOut, error, detail}` and `control {…}`, with the pre-existing `gateExit`/`controlExit` keys kept intact.
A new named check `gate.timeout` fails whenever `timedOut` is true, so a killed child can never be credited as a pass by an exit predicate that tolerates `null`.
The existing exit-status predicates are unchanged: `gate.exit.legal` still requires 0 with the kit, `gate.exit.not-passed` still requires 3 without it.

HONEST BOUND: on the PRE-FIX code a timed-out run was already REFUSED (null !== 0 and null !== 3), but it was not ATTRIBUTABLE — the only trace was `exit = null`. The new arms redden on pre-fix code because the `gate.timeout` check they name did not exist at all.
newTestArms: kit present + a TIMED-OUT run is refused (mustFail: gate.timeout)
kit absent + a TIMED-OUT run is refused (mustFail: gate.timeout)

findings.title: gate.report.parseable accepts non-report JSON shapes; its detail does not distinguish the failure modes.
findings.reviewerClaimNuance: The literal example does NOT reproduce on b0d9ecb7: `gate.report !== undefined && gate.report !== null` already refused a JSON `null`. The reproducible hole is ARRAYS and PRIMITIVES (`[]`, `42`, `"x"`, `true` all satisfied the predicate, and `reportShape`/`staticErrors` then read them as unreadable). The null arm is kept as a regression pin.
codeFacts: `reportCheck()` passes ONLY when `typeof report === 'object' && report !== null && !Array.isArray(report)`.

The detail distinguishes all four outcomes: 'report parsed as an object' / 'the gate wrote no --json report (the file is absent)' / 'the gate's --json report is unparsable: <message>' / 'the gate's --json report parsed as <null|an array|a number|a string|a boolean> — not a report object'.
`GateRun.reportProblem` is a discriminated union (`{kind:'missing'} | {kind:'unparsable', message}`), so 'missing' and 'unparsable' no longer collapse into one `undefined`.
Predicate table in code-red-proof-finding-b.log: OLD admits null=false, array=true, number=true, string=true, boolean=true, object=true; NEW admits only object=true.
newTestArms: kit present + a JSON null report is refused (mustFail: gate.report.parseable)
kit present + a JSON array report is refused (mustFail: gate.report.parseable)
kit present + an unparsable report is refused (mustFail: gate.report.parseable)
